why_how.text: Keep doors locked and windows closed near an aggressive driver, and leave enough space ahead to pull away from behind another vehicle.
Do not underestimate another driver’s capacity for aggression.

High-capacity roads are designed for heavy traffic and often have multiple lanes and traffic-management features, while low-capacity roads generally serve lighter flows with fewer features and lower speeds.
On a high-capacity road, move as far right or into another safe location as possible, stay buckled inside, activate hazard lamps, call nine one one and wait for responders.
On a lower-capacity road, first move to a safe location clear of passing traffic, using the right shoulder if possible.
If leaving is necessary and safe on a lower-capacity road, exit away from approaching traffic and move to a protected place such as behind a barrier or onto a sidewalk.
If a safe exit is unavailable, remain buckled inside, turn on hazard lamps and call nine one one for help.
On an Illinois toll road, move far onto the right shoulder if possible, remain belted inside, use hazard lamps and call star nine nine nine or nine one one while waiting for assistance.
